verdict.rationale: Both refactors preserve behavior. A also adds characterization tests, run against the original code first, that cover branches the existing suite missed: zero quantity, unknown coupon, VIP stacked on a coupon, the free-shipping threshold, per-line tax rounding, partial-reservation rollback, a failing receipt, and non-decline gateway errors. A's top-level flow keeps the decline handling and its raise visible inline, and it extracts pricing fully. B hides a raise inside a NoReturn helper, leaves the discount logic inline, adds no tests, and justifies its choices with a 'three-argument rule' that does not exist in the repository.
a_issues: Stock commit, coupon redeem and status update stay inline in process_order, while the release loop is extracted; minor asymmetry
Some characterization tests use local fake classes instead of the conftest fixtures (acceptable but slightly ad hoc)
b_issues: No tests added; the refactor relies only on the 9 existing tests plus an unshipped differential script
_abort_declined_payment hides the raise inside a NoReturn helper, making control flow in the except block less obvious
Coupon/VIP discount logic is left inline, so process_order is still only partially decomposed
Report cites a 'project's three-argument rule' that appears nowhere in the repository, and _abort_declined_payment itself takes three arguments
Very thin helpers such as _mark_paid and _commit_stock add indirection without much readability gain

verdict.rationale: Both refactors preserve behavior: the remaining helper splits are side-effect-free or keep the same order of effects. B first added characterization tests for the branches the suite did not cover, which is the right way to protect a production refactor. B's report also openly explains the reserved→order.items change, while A's report hides that same change and cites a three-argument rule that does not exist in the repo.
a_issues: No tests added for branches the suite misses (VIP, invalid coupon, free shipping, per-line rounding, partial reservation rollback, receipt failure), so the refactor is protected only by 9 tests and an unshipped differential run.
Report cites a 'project's three-argument rule' that does not appear anywhere in the repository.
Report says behavior is preserved but does not mention that the decline path now releases order.items instead of the reserved list.
Discount logic and receipt try/except stay inline, so process_order is only partly decomposed. _mark_paid and _commit_stock are thin wrappers that add little.
b_issues: Iterates order.items twice (once for subtotal, once for tax) and recomputes line_cents in two places, which duplicates a little logic.
Tax is now computed after the coupon check instead of before. This is harmless because it has no side effects, but it is a small reordering the report does not mention.
Post-charge steps (commit, redeem, mark paid) stay inline in process_order.
